original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read Model section 1 of the three-register bound and identify the exact excluded free operations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: Exact diagonal minimum for factors I + u y^T (u in R^n, y in K^n) over any K-algebra R when free GL_n(K) maps may appear anywhere in the word: t_K(d), the number of entries outside K^x. Answers open question 1 of research/f2-right-vector-diagonal-minimum.
scope_change_reason: The card asks whether a larger or nonabelian register model escapes the scoped three-register obstruction. This package settles a narrower open question left by research/f2-right-vector-diagonal-minimum: whether free scalar basis changes lower the right-vector diagonal count. The answer covers every group algebra F2[G] in the full nonidentity-label alphabet, so no nonabelian group gives a shorter diagonal there.
bottleneck_link: A legal diagonal shorter than t would be a new bit primitive. Free scalar mixing does not supply one in this alphabet; this is a side result and kappa is unchanged.
stop_rule: Prove the normal form, the kernel lemma and the matching construction; corroborate on three small rings (one nonabelian, one over F3) with exhaustive free-map searches; then stop.
evidence: PROOF.md is the argument. verify.py exhausts words of length at most 2 over F2[C2xC2] and at most 1 over F2[S3] and F3[x]/(x^2) at n=2, with every free map, checks every conjugate stays in the alphabet (93720 checks), checks the kernel lemma in 718128 cases, and checks the ring-valued sharpness witness.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: For a non-diagonal target M, is the minimum min over T in GL_n(K) of dim_K (M T - I) K^n?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It would give the exact cost of every target in this alphabet, not only diagonals.
open_questions.first_step: Test a permutation target over F2[C2] at n=2 against an exhaustive word search.
open_questions.blocked_by: The upper bound needs a factorization of I + C Y^T whose prefixes stay invertible; none is proved here.

open_questions.question: Which restricted label sets keep a count above t once free scalar mixing is allowed?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The Q8 {i,j} lower bounds use restricted labels; this package shows the full label set gives exactly t.
open_questions.first_step: Add one paid label outside {i,j} in F2[Q8] and recompute the single [zi] target.
open_questions.blocked_by: Nothing for the formal statement; native conversion remains unpriced.
